title: kith-chat: Message/set create accepts and validates attachment metadata
description:
What: Extend process_create in kith-chat/message.rs to parse, validate, and persist attachment metadata from Message/set create args.

Algorithm:
1. In process_create, after body/bodyType validation, extract optional attachments array from args: args.get("attachments").
2. Parse each attachment object: { blobId: String, filename: String, contentType: String, size: u64, sha256: String }.
3. Validate each attachment before message insert:
   a. validate_blob_id(&blob_id) — reject path traversal.
   b. filename: reject empty, reject containing ../ or / or \0 or \, reject len > 255.
   c. contentType: must contain exactly one /; reject empty; reject newlines; reject len > 256.
   d. size: must be <= 104_857_600.
   e. sha256: must be 64 lowercase hex chars.
   f. Verify blob exists in store.attachments().get_blob_meta(&blob_id) — reject unknown blobIds.
4. Limit: max 20 attachments per message. Reject if exceeded.
5. After message insert, for each attachment: store.attachments().insert(&blob_id, &msg_id, ...).
6. If any insert fails, rollback (use unchecked_transaction wrapping message insert + all attachment inserts).

Defensive rules: all validation before DB write; max attachment count limit; reject blobIds not previously uploaded; transaction atomic; never trust client-supplied size (store separately, verified at upload time).

Agent team: R reads existing process_create and AttachmentStore signatures; I implements; T writes unit tests: valid create with 1 attachment, invalid blobId rejected, filename with ../ rejected, contentType with newline rejected; V runs cargo test -p kith-chat + clippy.
